summary: Jitendra Nath Banerjea (1895–1966) was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, history, and archaeology. He studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri (~1916–1918) and served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (~1952–1959).

Jitendra Nath Mohanty (1928–2023) studied at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and University of Göttingen (Ph.D. ~1952–1954). A philosopher and Indologist, he taught at Calcutta, Burdwan, The New School, University of Oklahoma, and Temple University (1986–2012).
Jitsushyu Oshika (b. 1919) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He was educated at Tohoku University and held a professorship at Toyo University, attested in 1980–1981.

Jitsuzo Kuwabara (1871–1931) was a sinologist and historian who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1892–1896). He taught at the Third Higher School (1898–1899), Tokyo Higher Normal School (1899–1907), and Kyoto Imperial University (1909–1930).
Jiun Kubota (b. 1932) is a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied under Yamada Koun from circa 1970 to 1989 and ultimately succeeded him.

Jiyu Ren (1916–2009) studied at Peking University under Yongtong Tang and Lin He. An expert in philosophy and Buddhist and religious studies, he held posts at Peking University, the Chinese Academy of Sciences, and the National Library of China.

Jiyu-Kennett (1924–1996) studied at Durham University and Trinity Laban, and trained under teachers including Keidō Chisan Kōho. A Buddhist figure, she served as head priest at Unpuku-ji and founded Shasta Abbey, serving as abbess (~1970–1996).

Joachim Gentz is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He served as Junior Professor in Religious Studies at the University of Göttingen and as Reader in Chinese Studies at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2013).

Joachim Heinrich Campe (1746–1818) was a linguist and educator who studied at the University of Helmstedt (~1765–1768) and the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1768–1769). His students included Wilhelm von Humboldt.
Joachim Prandstetter is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed his Magister degree at the University of Vienna by 1994, studying under Gerhard Oberhammer.

Joachim Wach (1898–1955) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Munich, Berlin, Freiburg, Leipzig, and Heidelberg. He held posts at Leipzig, Brown University (1935–1946), and the University of Chicago Divinity School (1945–1955).

Joan Jiko Halifax (b. 1942) works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Tulane and Union Institute (PhD), held posts at Columbia, Miami, and Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, and founded the Ojai Foundation and Upaya Zen Center.

Joanna Gottfried Williams (1939–2022) was an Indology, art history, and archaeology scholar. She studied at Swarthmore College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University (1960–1969), and served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~1967–2016).
Joanna Macy (1929–2025) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She completed her studies at Wellesley College (~1946–1950) and Syracuse University (~1973–1978).

Joanne Punzo Waghorne is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago (~1971–1976). She held academic posts at UM-Boston (1975–1983), Bowdoin College (1983–1985), UNC Chapel Hill (1987–2002), and Syracuse University.

Joe Bransford Wilson is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Virginia (Ph.D. 1984). He taught at Virginia (1981–1985) and UNC Wilmington (attested 1994–2001).

Joe Cribb (b. 1947), educated at Queen Mary University of London, is an expert in numismatics and Central Asian and Indian history. He served as Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (1970–2010).

Joel Peter Brereton (b. 1948) is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Stanley Insler in 1971. He held academic posts at the University of Missouri (1999–2000) and the University of Texas at Austin (2004).
Joel Tatelman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Oxford in 1996 under the supervision of Alexis Sanderson.

Joerg Tuske is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held a post at the University of Cambridge (attested 1998) and served as an Associate Professor of Philosophy at Salisbury University (attested 2013).
